newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium lifts arrest warrant against Serge Dassault.
newsitem.headline: Belgium lifts arrest warrant against Serge Dassault.

text.p: The Belgian judiciary has lifted the international arrest warrant against French industrialist Serge Dassault, Belgian Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck said on Saturday.
But he denied that there had been political pressure and said Belgium had not received from France the documents it had requested to investigate bribery allegations against Dassault.
"The investigating magistrate has independently decided to lift the warrant...no political pressure was involved," De Clerck told Belgian radio BRTN.
"The decision was made in the context of the preparation of the trial and is no indication of guilt or innocence," he said.

A Belgian court in May 1996 issued the warrant for Dassault as part of an inquiry into claims Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) to political parties to secure a contract to fit air defence systems to Belgian F-16 jets in the late eighties.
Dassault, chairman of French aerospace firm Dassault Aviation, has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions for fear of being arrested.
Belgian authorities in May 1994 imprisoned Didier Pineau Valencienne, chairman of French electrical engineering group Schneider, for two weeks in a corruption probe.
The court of Liege, in eastern Belgium, issued the international arrest warrant against Dassault after his refusal to attend a hearing there.
But asked by French radio Europe 1 on Saturday whether he would be willing to testify now in Belgium, Dassault said: "I think yes, but we have to see under which conditions."
He refused to say why the Belgian judiciary had lifted the warrant.

It also remained unclear whether the new French government had agreed to give more information about the Dassault case to the Belgian judiciary. The Belgian government has tried for months to get key documents about the case from France.
De Clerck said earlier this year that the former French government had refused to hand over 11 documents to the Belgian authorities in the interest of France's national defence.
"No progress has been made in this area," De Clerck told BRTN on Saturday.
He added that Belgium continued to exert pressure on the new French government about the exchange of information in the investigation.
Several Belgian political parties are under investigation for allegedly accepting bribes from the French group.

In 1995, NATO secretary general Willy Claes, a Belgian economics minister in the late eighties, was forced to resign over bribes alleged to have been paid to his Socialist Party by Dassault and Italian helicopter maker Agusta Spa.
